reported.title: Running total overflows int, producing negative levels
reported.description: `total` is declared `int` on line 13, but it accumulates 40 ADC readings of up to 1023, so the sum can reach ~40920, far beyond the 32767 limit of a 16-bit int. The overflow wraps the sum negative, and averageMm() on line 28 then computes a large negative millimetre value, which is why the firmware printed -3856 mm while the injected level was ~4150 mm (off by ~8000 mm). Firmware printed -3856 mm at 1.02 s while the injected input was 4140.4 to 4169.8 mm: off by 7996.4 mm (tolerance ±40). 10 of 10 values were wrong.

reported.title: Lamp driven from overflowed average, so it never lights correctly
reported.description: showLamp() on line 33 compares averageMm() against FULL_MM, but averageMm() returns a negative value because of the int overflow in `total` (line 13/28). The comparison is therefore always false and D6 stays LOW even when the injected level is above 4200 mm, e.g. D6 was not HIGH for 1730 ms in the nominal ramp and 2420 ms in the max/min scenario. D6 was in the wrong state for 350 ms across 2 interval(s), first at 1.50 s: D6 was not HIGH for 180 ms while required (grace 1500 ms).

truth.description: The running sum of 40 ADC readings is a 16-bit int, which overflows once the level is above about 4000 mm, so the printed level turns negative and the lamp never lights

truth_for_judge.description: The running sum of 40 ADC readings is a 16-bit int, which overflows once the level is above about 4000 mm, so the printed level turns negative and the lamp never lights

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial values for '^level (-?\\d+) mm$' match the stimulus (tolerance 40) (Printed level tracks the probe)
D6 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when A2 >= 4200; LOW when A2 < 4200; within 1500 ms (Lamp at 4200 mm)

judge_input.spec:
- Level probe on A2 scaled at 1 mV per mm; full-level lamp on D6.
- Take one sample every 25 ms and average the last 40 into a level in millimetres. Fill the window at power-up so the first printed level is already valid.
- Print `level <mm> mm` every 1000 ms; the printed level must stay within ±40 mm of the injected level.
- Drive D6 HIGH when the averaged level is at or above 4200 mm; otherwise LOW, within 1500 ms.
- The probe reads up to 4800 mm.
